scene nodokahall1
: Oh. Well, hello there.
: To what do I owe the pleasure, Sensei?
: No pleasure involved, just here to kill some time.
: No pleasure involved? Not even a little bit?
: I mean...if you want there to be pleasure...
scene nodokahall2
: Of course I want there to be pleasure.
: Why else would I have this word-coated rectangular object in my hands?
: Weird way to say “book” but okay.
: What I mean to ask is why bother indulging yourself in anything if there is nothing to leech from it?
: We are all but leeches, Sensei. Digging our tiny, jagged teeth into anything they’ll latch onto in search of the essence of life.
: Weird way to say “blood” but okay again.
scene nodokahall3
: Would you at least agree that words without experience are meaningless?
: It’s something that appeared inside of this very rectangle and I’d be a liar if I were to say it didn’t provoke some impure thoughts in this old noggin of mine.
: You’re still in [high_school]. Your noggin is absolutely not “old.”
: No, it is not.
: But that calls into question exactly why I am reading this specific piece of literature despite having no experience in its subject matter.
: If words without experience are meaningless, shouldn’t these words, which I have no experience with, simply bounce off the walls of my brain without so much as leaving a minor bruise?
: Can brains even bruise?
: Probably? I can’t imagine it would feel very nice, though.
: What are you reading anyway?
scene nodokahall4
: “Lolita.” Are you familiar with it?
: Vaguely. I feel like I read that a long time ago but I’m kind of hazy on the details.
: I’m not surprised you’ve read it given your...demeanor so far.
: I’m sure the title itself is enough to give you an inkling of what the subject matter is, though.
: Sexual conduct is one thing, but do you believe you’d ever be able to fall in love with someone so much younger than you, Sensei?
: I prefer not discussing love whenever possible. It’s not exactly a cut and dry topic.
: Do you think you’d ever be able to love someone so much older?
scene nodokahall5
: I also prefer not discussing love whenever possible.
: It’s not exactly a cut and dry topic.
: I do yearn for the taboo, though. But I’m pretty sure the whole [incest] thing gave that away.
: Yeah, you’ve come across as kind of...freaky so far.
: I do? Whatever do you mean?
: I’m but an inexperienced, [adolescent] leech whose teeth aren’t sharp enough to latch onto anything.
: Perhaps I could try to take a bite out of you, Sensei? For practice.
: Like, right now?
: Just a little nibble. Quickly, before Uta sees us.
: That book is really getting to you, huh?
scene nodokahall6
: It is.
: I’m very easily fascinated by things most people aren’t able to experience in their own lives.
: Though, I suppose the idea of an illicit and inappropriate relationship may be a bit more common than I thought prior to attending [kumon_mi_high].
: So, yes. I can’t help but feel my heart begin to race at the thought of something like that.
: Maybe I’ll give it another go soon. It’s been a while since I’ve read anything, to be honest.
: That’s a shame. Literature can be a portal to different worlds and different lives.
: Your time would likely be better spent on literature you’re not currently living through, though.
: Are you suggesting something about me, Nodoka?
: If not suggesting, then recommending...as you have more than a handful of opportunities at your disposal.
: You’ve already confirmed some of your thoughts on the topic of manipulation. Surely you don’t only use that tactic for little, white lies.
: Is this your attempt at manipulating me?
: What would I possibly manipulate you into doing that you wouldn’t already do on your own?
: Reading more books.
scene nodokahall7
: Ahh, yes. The consumption of knowledge has become more taboo than any illicit relationship out there.
: It’s certainly starting to feel like that, at least.
scene nodokahall8
: I’m surprised you’ve managed to go so long without diving into a word-maze, though.
: Jesus, Nodoka. Just use the word “book.”
: Well now I’m just going to continue abstaining out of sheer spite.
: Of course you are...
: Futaba tells me you used to be a writer, Sensei.
: Why is it that you’ve given up on that?
: At this point, my brain is so all over the place that I feel like anything I write would come out twisted and indiscernible.
: So what? You should know better than anyone that the overflow of creative juices can lead to all sorts of amazing things.
: So can the overflow of less creative juices.
: Please explain to me in detail exactly which juices you are referring to, Sensei.
: Quickly, before Uta hears us and has to call her parents.
: You know about the parent thing too?
: I do. And your response has consequently confirmed that you’ve been involved in at least one sexual conversation with her.
: Nice.
: She’s an overly flirtatious part-time maid. It would be more surprising if I didn’t find myself in a conversation like that with her at least once.
: Ooooooh and you like maids as well.
: We should go to the cafe together sometime and prey upon those innocent girls.
: Think of how many soft, slender necks we could dig our teeth into.
: My [niece] works at that cafe, Nodoka.
scene nodokahall9
: Sensei...you’re really trying to excite me now, aren’t you?
: I feel like you are very easily excited.
: But not very easily satisfied.
: Remember that when the time comes for you to become my own Humbert Humbert.
scene nodokahall10
: Until then, though, I suppose I will continue to live inside of paper.
: Wait. I don’t remember much of “Lolita,” but I’m pretty sure I’m already that Humbert guy.
: We’re not at that part of the novel yet, Sensei.
: But perhaps, somewhere, some day, at a less miserable time, we may see each other again.
: Goodnight.
scene nodokahall11
Nodoka goes back into her room and leaves me standing in the hall, bewildered and mildly aroused.
That’s pretty much how half of our conversations end, though, so I’m not too shocked by it.
scene black
Either way, I decide to simply go home and rest.
But not until after knocking on her door several times to see if she was ready to skip further into our novel together.
